normal: No visible manufacturing defects; the part appears conforming.
defective: At least one visible manufacturing defect or anomaly.

normal: Extruded material forms a smooth, continuous strand or layer of even width, with clean straight edges and no blobs, gaps or thin spots.
defective: Extruded material is uneven: either too much material, with blobs, bulges, swelling or smeared excess, or too little material, with thin, broken or stringy strands, gaps and voids.
reason: The design images are close-ups of extruded strands and the defects are over- and under-extrusion; the generic text named no visible cue, so this names uneven width, excess blobs and thin gappy strands.

normal: Extruded material forms a smooth, continuous strand or layer of even width, with clean straight edges and no blobs, gaps or thin spots. Blur, glare, low contrast and a cluttered or dark background are normal and are not defects.
defective: Extruded material is uneven: either too much material, with blobs, bulges, swelling or smeared excess, or too little material, with thin, broken or stringy strands, gaps and voids.
reason: Several high-scored nominal images are blurry, glary or have busy dark backgrounds while the strand itself is even; the normal text now says these image conditions are not defects.

normal: Extruded material forms a smooth, continuous strand or layer of even width, about as wide as the nozzle tip it leaves, with clean straight edges and no blobs, gaps or thin spots.
defective: Extruded material is uneven: either too much material, wider than the nozzle tip, with blobs, bulges, swelling or smeared excess, or too little material, narrower than the nozzle tip, with thin, broken or stringy strands, gaps and voids.
reason: Many images show a nozzle tip with the strand below it, and the defect is excess or missing material; building on candidate 2, both texts now judge strand width against the nozzle tip.

normal: Extruded material forms a smooth, continuous strand or layer of even width, with straight parallel sides and no blobs, gaps or thin spots.
defective: Extruded material is uneven: either too much material, with blobs, bulges, swelling or smeared excess, or too little material, with thin, broken or stringy strands, gaps and voids. The outline of the material is rounded, bulbous, curved or tapering instead of straight-sided.
reason: Low-scored defects such as pale, washed-out strands still show rounded, teardrop or tapering outlines, while nominal strands have straight parallel sides; building on candidate 2, this adds the outline shape cue.

normal: The extruded strand carries the right amount of material: it is smooth, continuous and of even width.
defective: The extruded strand carries the wrong amount of material: too much, so it bulges or blobs, or too little, so it is thin, broken or has gaps.
reason: Candidates 3 to 5 added cues without a gain; this tests whether a shorter text focused only on the amount of material, the shared cause of over and under defects, ranks better than candidate 2's long list.
